alignments.note: Name to name.
Expressed copula; the clause is not verbless, so rules 53, 63 and 68 do not arise and the copula is not a supplied word to be placed.
Anarthrous Greek, so the supplied indefinite is an ordinary rule 7/51 helper on the noun it determines rather than an article's own determiner.

One Greek adjective rendered by an English phrase. The head is the stem word *passions*: ὁμοιοπαθής is unattested in the corpus, so rule 104 sends the query to the neighbouring class, and a privative-or-prefixed compound heads on its root word there — εὐπειθής → *easy to be entreated* on *entreated*, εὐάρεστος → *well pleasing* on *pleasing* — while the παθ- family heads on the παθ- word (τῶν παθημάτων → *the sufferings*). *like* glosses ὁμοιο- and *of* is the case helper. Heading on *like* is the competing reading and would take the prefix over the stem, which rule 104's analogies refuse. The verse note's alternative *nature* is not the ASV text and is not aligned.
Dative pronoun governed by the adjective, with its supplied case preposition riding along under rule 21's determinerless clause; no article stands to anchor *with*.
Expressed conjunction.
Inflected verb with its supplied subject pronoun; rule 9 heads on the lexical verb.

Cognate dative of manner (the verse note glosses it *with prayer*), which the ASV renders by the intensifying adverb *fervently*. Splitting it from the verb keeps rule 2's smallest defensible unit; rule 73's collapsed light-verb unit is not the case here, since προσεύχομαι is no verb of general sense and the ASV writes a separate English word for each element.

Nominalizing article of the articular infinitive, unrepresented under rules 61 and 23. Rule 61 hands the English clause-introducer to a governing preposition, and none is expressed here, so nothing falls to the article; rule 85 then puts the supplied complementizer *that* on the non-finite complement it introduces. Giving *that* to τοῦ by analogy with rule 61's preposition case is the competing reading, and rule 61 forecloses it by aligning the article only where the ASV writes a determiner of its own.

The ASV expands the infinitive into a finite clause; rule 85 gives the supplied complementizer *that* to the non-finite complement, and the supplied subject and modal ride with it under rules 7 and 9. Discontinuous around *not* under rule 15, headed on the lexical verb under rule 17.
Ordinary negative μή aligned to *not*; no negative indefinite stands, so rules 59 and 79 do not apply, and rule 44's interrogative particle is not in question.
Expressed conjunction.
Finite verb with its supplied subject pronoun, headed on the lexical verb.
Ordinary negative aligned to *not*; no negative indefinite follows, so rule 41 does not empty it.
Preposition to preposition under rule 36.
Article to *the* under rule 19; the preposition is expressed and keeps its own word, so no case preposition rides with the article under rule 21.
Noun stands alone, its determiner taken by the article under rule 21.

Accusative of duration; the supplied case preposition *for* rides with the noun under rule 21's determinerless clause, since no article stands to anchor it, discontinuously around *three* under rule 15.
Numeral split from its noun under rule 26.
Expressed conjunction joining the two duration phrases; rule 29's helper *and* is not in question here, since the Greek writes the conjunction.
Numeral split from its noun under rule 26; the ASV puts it before the noun, and rule 15 permits the reordering.
Noun stands alone.

review_notes: Reviewed and kept unchanged: all 22 units of the accepted alignment stand, with three notes enriched (s004's head, s009's competing reading, s022's reordering rule citation). No edges, statuses or heads were changed.
All 22 source and 31 target ids are partitioned exactly once; s009 is the only unrepresented unit and there are no added units.

s004 ὁμοιοπαθής → *of like passions* is the one head worth checking. The lexeme is unattested in the corpus, so rule 104 governs: the neighbouring-class query (compound prefix-plus-stem adjectives, and the παθ- root family) heads the stem word, giving *passions*. A head on *like* would take the prefix over the stem and is the reading rule 104's analogies refuse.

s007 προσευχῇ → *fervently* and s008 → *he prayed* stay split rather than joined. Rule 73 wants a verb of general sense collapsed by the ASV into a single English verb; προσεύχομαι carries its own lexical content and the ASV writes a separate word for each element, so rule 2 applies.

s009 τοῦ is unrepresented and the supplied *that* goes to the infinitive under rule 85. Rule 61 gives a clause-introducer to a governing preposition, and none is expressed here, so the article has nothing to take; the competing reading that τοῦ carries *that* as the nominalizer is named in the unit note.

*for* at t026 and *with* at t008 are both supplied case prepositions on determinerless phrases, so rule 21's determinerless clause keeps each with its own noun or pronoun rather than manufacturing an article-borne *for the* or *with the*.
